page: Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is a memory-optimized and storage-capable server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this virtual machine features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is a key feature of this instance, which bundles 2880 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core processing and memory throughput. The L4aos_v4 demonstrates strong single-core performance, scoring in the top 25% for both stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core evaluations. Text processing is also a strong point. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are more limited. Multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the average category, while memory read bandwidth for both small and large blocks is weak, landing in the bottom 25%. Database operations and software compilation benchmarks also register in the lower 25% tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the L4aos_v4 offers high local storage density and substantial memory capacity per vCPU, making it a viable option for workloads requiring large temporary datasets without the premium cost of larger compute-heavy instances. However, the tradeoff lies in its weak memory read speeds and lower database operation performance, which may bottleneck memory-bound or highly concurrent transactional databases. This server is best suited for memory-intensive single-threaded tasks, text processing, light LLM inference using small models, and workloads that benefit from large local storage capacity but do not demand extreme memory bandwidth.
